text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Russian Foreign Minister Primakov says Syria has no intention of attacking Israel.
- Police gearing for formation of new underground movement by right-wing radicals.
- Defence Minister Mordechai decides to continue West Bank and Gaza closure because of warnings of terror attacks.
- Suspected killer of Palestinian boy to be charged with manslaughter, offence that carries a maximum 20-year prison term.
- Netanyahu tells Israeli general who also serves as peace negotiator that he erred in meeting leaders of the Israeli opposition without permission.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu and Mordechai to decide today the future of Major General Shahor, Israeli peace negotiator who met Israeli opposition leaders.
- Opinion poll shows 85 percent of Israelis back Clinton.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Israel and Syria exchange messages via Russian Foreign Minister Primakov.
- Opinion poll shows 87 percent of Israelis back Clinton.
- "I'm sorry about the boy, but I didn't kill him," says suspected Israeli killer of 11-year-old Palestinian.
GLOBES
- Preparations under way to offer 20 percent stake in Bank Leumi on London and New York stock exchanges.
- Heavy sentences and fines for five former Israel Discount Bank employees and a businessman in stock manipulation trial.
- Elbit wins $100 million tender for upgrading Romanian cargo helicopters.
JERUSALEM POST
- No Syrian plans for attack, Primakov tells Netanyahu.
- Netanyahu says Hebron's Jewish community will never be uprooted.
- Egypt not invited heads of state to economic parley.
- Israeli to be charged with murder of Palestinian boy.
- Heavy jail terms and fines for Bank Discount stock manipulators.
- Closure of West Bank and Gaza to continue, but eased slightly.
